author: WILL BONTRAGER
title: Local youth bowler qualifies for nationals for the second year - NewsBreak
text:
By WILL BONTRAGER ,
13 hours ago
WILMINGTON, Del. — Abigail Ticknor, a 12-year-old bowler from Millington, Md., heads back to the Junior Gold Championships, securing her spot at a qualifying tournament at Pleasant Hill Lanes in Wilmington on Dec. 7.
Her father, Phil, told the Kent County News the 2026 Junior Gold Championships will be held at 10 bowling centers in and around Minneapolis and brings together qualified youth bowlers from across the country each summer for national championships in U12 boys, U12 girls, U14 boys, U14 girls, U16 boys, U16 girls, U18 boys, and U18 girls.
Ticknor qualified by finishing in third place among 14 bowlers in a combined U14 boys and U14 girls category at Pleasant Hill.
"She was first among nine U14 bowlers who had not previously qualified earlier this season," Phil said. "She secured the first of two available spots to nationals, bowling a total score of 882 across six games on a difficult PBA Bear oil pattern. Her individual game scores were 129, 177, 161, 134, 147, and 134 and moved into position for the first qualifying spot after the third game and never relinquished it."
Most impressive, Ticknor was one of only three girls competing in the U14 division and finished with the highest score among them, finishing behind only two boys who had already secured their spots to Junior Gold Nationals earlier this season.
Ticknor made her Junior Gold Championships debut this past July in Green Bay, Wis., where she finished 51st out of 107 entrants in the U12 Girls category.
A seventh-grader at Kent County Middle School, Ticknor bowls in the Varsity Division of the Doverama Dragons Youth League in Dover, Del.
The 2026 Junior Gold Championships will be held in the Minneapolis area July 13-18.
